entries.definition: machine-learning inference performed under about one milliwatt of power, typically on microcontrollers, DSPs, or small neural-network accelerators
devices that run at roughly 10-250 MHz and under 50 mW, with memory two orders of magnitude smaller than smartphone- or GPU-class systems
entries.notes: MCU used interchangeably after definition, not as a forbidden synonym -- it is the standard abbreviation for the same defined term.

entries.definition: the specific piece of hardware being benchmarked in a given submission
the open-source neural-network runtime used to execute every reference implementation on the reference board
converting an already-trained model to lower-precision numerics (e.g., 8-bit integers) without retraining
training a model while simulating low-precision numerics, rather than quantizing only after training
the suite's latency score: how many forward passes the device completes per second, taken as the median of five timed runs
closed = same model, dataset, and quality target as the reference, quantization only; open = model/training/dataset may change, but the same test set still measures accuracy
a convolution factored into a per-channel (depthwise) step and a 1x1 (pointwise) step, used to cut parameters and compute versus a standard convolution
a group of residual (skip-connection) blocks at one feature-map resolution, as in ResNet
a time-frequency representation of audio, with frequency binned on a perceptual (mel) scale and log-scaled energy
area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve; a threshold-free measure of how well a score separates two classes
entries.notes: assumed known without a full gloss for mode A/B; a one-clause reminder is still given because the source paper's 'parameterless' framing is otherwise unexplained.

entries.definition: a free, open, royalty-free instruction-set architecture (as opposed to a proprietary one)
reconfigurable hardware whose logic circuits can be redefined after manufacturing, as opposed to fixed silicon

one_term_per_concept_check: passed -- 'microcontroller-class hardware' is used consistently rather than alternating with 'edge device' or 'embedded system'; 'the suite' is used consistently rather than alternating with 'the framework' or 'the benchmark' once introduced.
acronym_frequency_check: DUT (3x), TFLM (4x), PTQ (5x), IPS (3x), AUC-ROC (4x), FPGA (2x), QAT (2x) are each used below the skill's informal '>=3 uses' guideline in one or two cases (QAT, FPGA); these are kept as acronyms anyway because they name widely-recognized, load-bearing technical objects (a training regime, a hardware class) rather than a project-specific shorthand, and each is spelled out in full at first use.
